instruction:
An archive stores Portuguese event logs as local calendar timestamps, without an offset or a fold flag. Before upgrading from IANA tzdb 2024a to 2024b, identify precisely which local timestamp ranges would acquire a different set of possible UTC interpretations.

Scope: every timezone whose country-code column includes PT in tzdb 2024b's zone1970.tab, and local timestamps from 1992-01-01T00:00:00 inclusive to 1994-01-01T00:00:00 exclusive. Compare the published, unmodified 2024a and 2024b data. Treat these as database semantics, including their historical assumptions, rather than attempting to establish historical legal truth. Use ordinary POSIX time, without leap seconds.

For each local timestamp, consider ALL UTC instants that convert to it under each release. Represent that set by the corresponding UTC offsets (local time minus UTC); an empty set means that local timestamp does not exist, and two offsets mean it is repeated. Do not choose an earlier/later occurrence or normalize a nonexistent time. Abbreviation-only or DST-flag-only differences do not count.

Return every maximal half-open local interval [start_local,end_local) for which the old and new offset sets differ, splitting whenever either set changes. Omit intervals and timezones with no difference. Adjacent intervals with identical pairs of sets must be merged. Sort by timezone name, then start_local.

Return only a table with these five columns:
zone | start_local | end_local | offsets_2024a | offsets_2024b
Use the timezone identifiers from the scoped table, local endpoints YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS (no Z), and sets of signed HH:MM offsets in braces separated by semicolons, e.g. {-02:00;+00:00}. Use {} for an empty set. These offset examples are format examples, not candidate answers.
